title: Weights governance and profile release runway
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end, auditable pipeline that takes community weights from intake to a pinned production-ready model profile while enforcing governance rules and fast fail-safes. This ticket scopes the core runway: manifest verification, deterministic conversion (shard-aware normalization -> canonical artifact), automated smoke and perf validation, model fingerprinting and version pin creation, and the profile publish step that writes to the catalog and notifies Console + telemetry.

Why this matters: Currently model admission requires significant manual steps and ad-hoc checks. We need a repeatable flow to reduce onboarding latency, prevent unsafe artifacts from reaching serving, and produce consistent performance profiles for routing and SLOs.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Signed manifest + provenance check completed automatically for a given weight bundle (GCS/HF/OSS).
- Deterministic conversion tool produces canonical artifact (single canonical file per commit) with reproducible VHash (content + architecture + conversion flags).
- Automated preflight: functional smoke (generation correctness), token-determinism check (seeded tokens), and microbenchmarks (latency @ 1/8/32 tokens, peak memory) pass against per-model thresholds.
- Failing preflight quarantines the artifact and creates a remediation checklist; passing artifacts are assigned a pin (semantic version + VHash) and published to model-catalog with performance profile attached.
- Publish emits telemetry events (profiling metrics, conversion warnings, security flags) to the infra-data pipeline and creates Console card with quick links to PRs and artifacts.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement rollout automation (canary/A-B) or Dedicated capacity routing rules — only the admission-to-publish path. Quantization pipelines will be invoked as a downstream job, not part of the canonical conversion step in this ticket.

Implementation notes / proposed approach:
1) Intake gate: signed-manifest verification (PGP/JWT), SBOM extraction, and virus/entropy heuristics. Reject unsigned or malformed manifests. Link to spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q-onboard-manifest-spec (confluence replacement).
2) Conversion: introduce "canon-convert" tool that normalizes sharded checkpoints (supports GGUF, SAFETENSORS, HF sharded states) into a normalized canonical package. Record conversion flags and deterministic seed. Output is a single artifact and a VHash. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canon-convert/pull/88.
3) Preflight suite: containerized runner that executes: small generation smoke (sanity prompts), deterministic repeat-run, and perf microbench (3 sizes). Thresholds pulled from model-profile-template. Runs on a dedicated preflight pool with GPU type label matching requested serving tier.
4) Governance: artifacts that fail security checks go to quarantined storage path and create ENG ticket with triage checklist. Artifacts that pass get pinned with semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR+VHash) and published to the catalog service with metadata (provenance, conversion flags, perf metrics).
5) Publish: catalog write + Console patch that creates a "Model card" entry with links to artifacts, telemetry dashboard, and a reconciliation job to verify catalog -> runtime mapping.

Open design trade-offs considered:
- Canonical format: ONNX vs GGUF vs Redwood internal. We pick GGUF-first for OSS compatibility and smaller friction for quantized variants; fallback conversion to internal runtime format happens downstream in the runtime ingestion pipeline.
- Determinism: strict bitwise determinism is costly; we enforce seed-determinism for functional tests and low-variance tolerances for perf numbers.
- Security gating: strictness will cause more quarantines initially; plan a staged rollout with a "permissive" training window for community models to gather telemetry before enforcing hard rejects.

Acceptance tests (manual & automated):
- End-to-end e2e test with a small Llama-style toy model that goes through intake -> conversion -> preflight -> pinned publish.
- Synthetic negative test: corrupt manifest or manipulated weights should fail intake and generate ENG ticket.
- Perf regression test using baseline model to assert microbenchmark within 15% of profile.

Links / artefacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canon-convert/pull/88
- Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q-onboard-manifest-spec
- Console placeholder card: https://console.redwood.ai/models?pending=1
comments: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Verified GGUF->canon conversion keeps tokenizer mappings intact for multi-embedding tokenizers. Prototype code in PR #88. — Diego
2026-03-04: Security review (initial) noted missing SBOM extraction for fused ops; added step to extract operator list during conversion. Action: add op-whitelist check. — Priya (Security)

2026-03-06: Ran preflight on 3 community submissions; two were quarantined due to manifest signature mismatch and one passed but had a 22% slower perf than baseline (investigating quantization flags). Created ENG-36120 as follow-up for conversion flag heuristics.
2026-03-08: Decided to expose VHash in model-catalog API (field: vhash) and include conversion_flags in catalog metadata. Diego to update catalog contract in runtime-1.20 release PR.
2026-03-10: Demo to PMs/Design scheduled 2026-03-12. Preparing runbook for quarantined artifact triage. — Aisha
